A total of 24 young boxers from the four sporting zones of Ogun State are preparing to make their debut at the maiden RIYE U17 Boxing Circuit, holding on Friday, October 30, 2026, at the Alake Sports Centre, Ijeja, Abeokuta. The event is organised by Hon. Tunde Delu under the Young Athletes Yield Initiative and designed to give young boxers a platform to showcase their skills, gain valuable competitive experience and begin their journey towards a career in the sport. Athletes, coaches, sports administrators and boxing enthusiasts are expected to attend what the organisers describe as a celebration of grassroots sports development. Beyond the competition and prizes, the initiative seeks to identify promising talents from Remo, Ijebu, Yewa and Egba, giving them an opportunity to develop their abilities and pursue their sporting dreams. The venue was among the facilities reconstructed ahead of the 2024 National Sports Festival, also known as the Gateway Games, which Ogun State hosted. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Five Nigerian pugilists storm African Championships finals MTN backs grassroots sports, gives Ogun school N1.5m Ogun assembly passes state police bill Shoyombo Anuoluwapo Daniella, nicknamed “Beast”, is one of the young female boxers preparing to step into the ring. The 16-year-old weighs 60kg and was born on December 16, 2009. She will be looking to demonstrate her skills and competitive spirit when the young boxers converge in Abeokuta. Ajadi Sulaimon, popularly known as “Sula”, is a male boxer who weighs 49kg and was born on February 12, 2011. The 15-year-old is among the talents looking forward to testing his abilities against his peers. Olaoye Esther, nicknamed “Iron Lady”, is a female boxer who weighs 48kg. The 16-year-old will aim to make the most of the platform to showcase her talent and determination. Alayande Rokeebat, nicknamed “Slow Poison”, a female boxer who weighs 48kg, is 17 years old and will be looking to showcase her boxing ability, determination and competitive spirit as she joins other young talents at the maiden circuit. Hassan Khadijat, popularly known as “Kay Star”, is a female boxer, weighs 50kg, and the 15-year-old is among the young athletes preparing to seize the opportunity to display her talent and gain valuable competitive experience. The organisers have assured that no stone will be left unturned in ensuring that the circuit is top-notch in every sphere. Peter Akinbo Peter, who has been covering sports for PUNCH for close to two years, focuses on combat sports reporting, special features and human angle stories
